title: Heat Pump Rebates in Mississauga 2026: What Gas and Electric Homes Get
desc: Mississauga heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: $500 per ton for gas homes, $1,250 per ton for electric, oil, propane and wood, and the pre-approval rule.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Mississauga has 244,575 households and 70% own. The heat pump rebate is the most generous in the program for homes that do not heat with gas, and modest for those that do.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Mississauga
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: About 62% of Mississauga households live in a house type the program accepts, and 27% live in tall apartments, which it excludes. The 2021 Census counts 7,880 households in duplexes. The requirements document allows a unit in a duplex, triplex or stacked townhome to apply if it has its own heating system and meter, but the web page lists only houses, so confirm with the program.
What the contractor must send first

Before installation, the contractor submits an itemized work order, photos of the existing heating system and its nameplate, a signed participant agreement and the NRCan sizing form for each outdoor unit. For electric homes, the photos must show baseboards in at least three areas. Written approval comes back before work begins. A Mississauga owner should ask the contractor for a copy of the approval.

A home that already has a heat pump used for space heating is not eligible, and replacing one earns nothing. If you added a ductless unit a few years ago and now want a whole-home system, ask the program how the first unit affects eligibility before you commit.

Rebates are paid on rated heating capacity at 8.3°C, with 12,000 BTU/h equal to one ton. A 2-ton system pays $2,500 to an electric home, $1,000 to a gas home. A 5-ton system pays $6,250 and $2,000. Use the capacity on the NRCan listing, not the model's marketing tonnage, to check the number.

Keep the signed participant agreement, the pre-installation approval, the itemized final invoice and the post-installation approval notice together. If the cheque is late or a question comes up, those four documents answer it. The contractor files the applications, but the rebate is yours, so having copies is your protection.
claim_steps: Check your main heating fuel and whether the house already has a heat pump.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
faq: How much does a 3-ton system pay a Mississauga gas home?
Do I need a home energy assessment?
Yes, at $500 per ton up to $2,000.
